_refresh: Properties: get_design_context on the node. Geometry: get_metadata (coords are absolute within the 1440x792 frame — sum the parent offsets).

_sources.get_design_context: generated React/Tailwind — fills, borders, radii, padding, type
_sources.get_metadata: XML geometry — x, y, width, height only

_rule: Assert only what a source states outright. Where the two sources disagree, skip the property and record why in _skipped rather than picking one.
_assertionRule: Assert only quantities the DESIGN determines — proportions, spacing, colour, type, radii, behaviour thresholds. Never assert quantities CONTENT determines — item counts, list totals, text-derived sizes, or any position downstream of them. Three corollaries, each paid for by a withdrawn assertion: (1) LISTS — assert the last item only where the list's length is fixed by the design. The five Library categories are hardcoded in Sidebar.jsx and match Figma, so the Trash row is assertable; .sb-more was not, because it compared Figma's five mock collections against the fixture's seven. A first-item assertion is only an origin check and is blind to accumulation — so where the last item is not assertable, the accumulation is not either, and that is a limit to state rather than to work around. (2) ANCHORED EDGES — for a text-sized box assert the edge the design anchors, not the one its glyphs move, and verify the edge really is anchored: .sb-count's trailing edge is fixed by its row, .seg's is not because it sits left of another text-sized box. (3) ACCUMULATION — an accumulated position is assertable only if every term in it is design-determined. Masonry card 8's y accumulates media heights chosen by a hash of the bookmark id, so it measured the fixture, not the app. Full statement: tools/visual-diff/README.md, 'What may be asserted'.

_notAssertable.collections rows: Count is fixture data — Figma draws 5 mock collections plus ••• More, the fixture seeds 7. Withdrawn 2026-07-28.
_notAssertable.masonry accumulation: Card 8's y accumulates per-card media heights, and a card's aspect bucket comes from a hash of its bookmark id. Withdrawn 2026-07-28; the finding it produced is recorded on .card-media as _cardAspectDrift. The design-determined alternative — the third column's x, which accumulates two column widths and two gutters — is also not clean: Figma's own frame pads 20px on the left and 21px on the right, so its columns imply 365.0 where the app computes 365.33, and the 0.67px difference is the design's rounding rather than the app's.
_notAssertable.tags: Figma's Tags Section (5181:148) and tag Section items (5270:138) are hidden, and the fixture renders no tags with count > 0. No list on either side.
_notAssertable.text-derived widths: .seg's width and right edge, .ask-chip's width, .sb-count's width and x. All move with glyph metrics. Where the design anchors an edge, that edge is asserted instead.

_strokeRule: Figma strokes do not consume layout; a CSS border on a border-box container does. Where the app draws a Figma stroke as a border, every Figma coordinate measured across that border is off by the border width, and the SPEC is adjusted — not the app. Record it as _rect._adjust with a _why. Strokes drawn as outline/box-shadow (e.g. .card-media) consume no layout and need no adjustment. Full rule: tools/visual-diff/README.md, 'Strokes and layout'.

_skipped.padding: get_design_context generates py-[14px]; get_metadata places the chip 12px from the frame top. Both cannot hold, so neither is asserted.
_skipped.effective background: The fill is 92% translucent over a backdrop-filter blur, so the composited value depends on blur parameters that have not been compared against Figma's own blur vector (5181:539). Left unasserted deliberately; the residual ask-bar colour difference stays a lead.

.ask-chip._note: Width deliberately not asserted — the chip is sized by its label. x is asserted because the chip is the first flex child of .ask, so its leading edge is design-determined.

.sb-row.is-active._name: Category Item (Everything, active — FIRST library row)
.sb-row.is-active._pairedWith: .sb-scroll > button:nth-of-type(5) — see that entry for why the last row is asserted too.

_adjust._why: Stroke rule. .sb draws Figma's 1px right stroke as border-right on a border-box box, so its content box is 264-20-20-1 = 223 and every width:100% child is 1px narrower than Figma's 224. Adjusting the spec keeps the app's symmetric 20px inner padding, which Figma's non-layout stroke actually breaks (its row leaves 19px on the right, 20px on the left).

.sb-scroll > button:nth-of-type(5)._note: LAST item of a repeated list, deliberately. Asserting the FIRST item of a mapped list passes whenever the container origin is right, and hides every per-item accumulation below it — which is exactly how an 8px row-gap omission survived a passing sidebar audit. Figma spaces category rows 40px apart (5181:44 children at y = 0, 40, 80, 120, 160); absolute y = 70 + 160.

_adjust._why: Stroke rule. Figma's view-mode frame is 32 tall (4 + 24 + 4) with a non-layout stroke; the app draws that stroke as a 1px border, so with box-sizing: border-box the control is 34 tall. The topbar centres it either way — both land centred on y=35 — so the extra 2px of height puts its top edge 1px higher. Design-determined, unlike its horizontal position.

.seg._note: Width/height and horizontal position deliberately not asserted: the control is sized by its button text, and its right edge is downstream of .btn-new's glyph width (measured 60.56 against Figma's 60), so neither edge is anchored to anything the design fixes. Vertical position IS design-determined and is asserted, with the stroke adjustment.

.card-media._pairedWith: .masonry-item:nth-child(8) .card-media — a first-item assertion only proves the grid ORIGIN is right. The last-card assertion is what proves the run of cards between them accumulates correctly.

_skipped.height: get_metadata gives 195, implying aspect 1.872. That is not one of the app's CARD_ASPECTS buckets (format.js), so asserting it would test the fixture's bucket choice rather than the app. The x/y assertion still catches where the grid starts.
_skipped.background-color: The design fills the thumbnail with an image, so no background colour is stated; the app's --surface shows only where an image is missing.

.card-media._note: Figma states a 1px stroke. The app renders it as outline with outline-offset:-1px rather than a border — visually equivalent and arguably better, since a border would inset the image. Asserted on the property the app actually uses.
.card-media._cardAspectDrift: Measured 2026-07-28 and left unasserted: the app's grid runs 25.58px longer than the design by the third card in column 1 (Figma 715, app 740.58). Card 1's media is 205.23 against Figma's 195 and card 4's is 365.33 against 350, because the design's thumbnail proportions are 365/195 = 1.872 and 365/350 = 1.043 and CARD_ASPECTS (format.js) has neither — nearest buckets are 1.78 and 1.0. Recorded rather than asserted because which bucket a card gets comes from a hash of its bookmark id, so the assertion measured the fixture. See _notAssertable.

.sb._note: Spec supplied by Mike 2026-07-28: #F6F3F3 at 1% over the global #080808 background, with a #FAFFE6 6% stroke.

_effectiveBackground._why: Translucent fill: Chromium's blend does not match arithmetic compositing, and only the painted value can match what the colour sampler sees.

.content._note: .content is transparent; the canvas colour comes from an ancestor, so only the composited value is meaningful here.

_effectiveBackground._why: The canvas is opaque so arithmetic compositing is exact; sampling would return a card, since .content is full of them.

.sb-row.is-active .sb-count._note: `right` is asserted instead of `x`: the badge is the last flex child of .sb-row with .sb-row-name flexing, so its trailing edge is anchored and its leading edge floats with the digit count. Asserting x measured glyph width, the same mistake as asserting width.

_skipped.color: get_design_context puts the label at acid/900 #0d1d00 with opacity 0.8 applied separately; the app bakes opacity 0.9 into the element, so the two are not directly comparable.

_adjust._why: Stroke rule — the badge is anchored to .sb-row's trailing edge, and that row's content box lost 1px to .sb's border-right (see .sb-row.is-active). Figma right = 210 + 26.
